intro_html: Choose chilled/thawed or frozen explicitly. Start timing after the bag is submerged and the preheated bath has recovered. Measure the thickest part and keep portions in one layer. The calculator distinguishes meat heating, soft-salmon recipe times and lean-fish pasteurization.

after_html: Asparagus finish (optional): dry well, then blister 30–60 sec in a very hot pan.
Cauliflower finish (optional): drain liquid, then roast or broil 4–6 min for color. Pairs well with a knob of butter and ½–1 tsp curry powder per ~300 g in the bag.
Beets: 85 °C, 1½–4 h by size — see Sous vide beets.
rows: 15 min default. Use 18–20 min if clumped/tightly packed.
Mostly heat-through + slight tenderizing. Single layer cooks best.
Bag with butter + curry powder. Single layer; weigh down if needed.

after_html: Finish: pat dry, then hard sear 30–60 sec/side for color.

after_html: Bagging: 2 per bag for very thick drumsticks; 3 per bag OK if mostly single-layer. Finish: dry thoroughly, broil 4–8 min total, flip once; apply sugary sauces late.
rows: Add ~1 h if very thick or tightly packed.

after_html: Sear: optional cool-in-bag 5–10 min, pat very dry, then 30–60 sec/side in screaming-hot pan + neutral oil. Add butter only at the end (15–30 sec baste).
These steak windows are practical texture guides, not pasteurization schedules. For other thicknesses, use the meat heat-through calculator above.

after_html: Finish: dry well, brush thin sauce, then broil 4–8 min total (flip once). If sauce is sweet, apply late and watch constantly.
For these long texture cooks, use the same broad window from chilled or frozen. Frozen pieces must be individually separated; a solid frozen bundle or unusually large cut needs a separate schedule.

after_html: Use salmon suitable for undercooked service with supplier-confirmed parasite controls. Ordinary freezer storage does not establish parasite destruction. Unpasteurized fish is unsuitable for pregnant or immunocompromised people.
